properties.description: Washington State Ferries proposes to install electrical equipment to support future operation of hybrid diesel-electric ferry vessels at the Seattle Terminal on Elliott Bay. The project includes installing the following components: electrical equipment on the uplands at Pier 48 to connect to existing Seattle City Light electrical feeders; two submarine conduits in Elliott Bay from Pier 48 uplands to the Seattle Terminal pier; new decking on the Seattle Terminal pier to support on-deck electrical equipment within new protective canopies; two in-water vessel charging system (VCS) platforms to support hybrid vessels at Seattle Terminal Slips 1 and 3; protective dolphins for the VCS platforms; and two overwater catwalks to allow maintenance access from the pier to the VCS platforms. Also included is removal of two existing floating concrete dolphins and timber debris from the seafloor. See submitted project narrative and site plan for additional details.

properties.description:
The area under our waterfront deck (9ft x12ft) was backfilled with construction debris, beach sand and clay chunks. The debris included several unsightly large chunks of concrete  leaning against the support for the deck. Additionally, there is an old drainage pipe that is failing. We want to clear the debris, improve and re-connect the drainage, and add a small  wood and post wall (3ft high x12 ft wide), to hide the foundation and drainage pipes and provide storage for our kayak and SUP. There are existing concrete stairs and a large concrete chunks which we want to mortar together to make a sitting area and walkway access for SUP storage. 

The face of the seawall has some cracks, but is otherwise sound. We would like to fill the voids with concrete patch to slow the degradation of the surface. 

On the east boundary of our property, along the driveway, we want to move the east fence line 4 feet out, to the property line. This will involve removing a 4'x20' paved strip which will then be maintained as permeable landscaping. Changes to the fence line does not impact the neighbors view.  

The purpose of the moving the fence line is to secure our property, enclose our dog, provide privacy and visibly establish our ownership. This is, in part, a response to 5 years of litigation by our neighbor who attempted to adversely possess that portion of our property which was outside the original fence line. She lost in court twice, at great expense to all concerned. Her home is built within 8 feet of our mutual north-south property line. A later remodel added stairs and landing 1 foot from the property line, affording us little privacy and fueling her desire for our land. Her home has been a rental property for 5 years and is about to go on the market. We do not want to go through this again with a new neighbor. 

Thank you.

There is a single moorage float off of the eastern pier that is accessed via a wooden ramp from the eastern pier.  The proposed project is to replace the existing solid decked moorage float built on large logs with a new fully grated moorage float built on solid plastic, foam filled flotation tubs.  The existing mooring pile and access ramp to the moorage float will be retained.  The new float will be the same size, location and configuration as the existing moorage float avoiding impacts to lake bottom below.  No additional work is proposed.

properties.description:
Address is between 1101 Alaskan Way and 1201 Alaskan Way.

Piers 55 & 56 LLC proposes to remove approximately 2,200 SF of the existing Pier 55.5's east apron and with it the demolition of (38) creosote treated timber piles and (10) steel stub pile repairs. The existing timber pier will be replaced with a pier consisting of (8) 20-inch-diameter vertical steel pipe piles, (4) 20-inch-diameter batter steel pipe piles, and (4) 24-inch-diameter vertical steel pipe piles supporting cast-in-place concrete pile caps with precast concrete deck panels. Additionally (2) 10-inch-diameter vertical steel pipe piles will be driven with a vibratory hammer at the north and south ends of the Pier 55.5 east apron underneath Piers 56 and 55, respectively. The new concrete deck will be precast concrete panels designed to the International Building Code (IBC) occupancy requirements of 100 psf live load and to accommodate an AASHTO H10 vehicle design criteria. The center bent of the proposed new pier, approximately a sixth of the overall square footage, will also be designed to accommodate a future 150-ton crawler crane which will support the Pier's long-term development plans of maintenance and replacement of Pier 55 and other portions of Pier 55.5.

There will be a reduction in the overall number of piles used in the proposed improvements to the existing pier. The overall footprint of the proposed pier will remain the same as the existing pier; therefore, no new overwater coverage would be created. Existing timber elements have deteriorated and the structure is in need of maintenance or replacement to increase public safety and to bring the pier to current building codes, as pier does not meet current seismic design codes. In addition, a majority of the east apron of Pier 55.5 is currently closed off from all access as it has been deemed a public safety hazard due to damage from the Elliot Bay Seawall Project and construction.
